messages:
alex_support: Heads-up — support ticket from Maria (PRO acct) reporting malformed JSON from our streaming JSON mode when calling via SSE behind their proxy. They see partial JSON (missing closing brace) and the consumer fails to parse. Repro steps + snippet below, can eng-runtime / SRE weigh in? :thinking:

maria_cust: Repro is simple. We call the API with Accept: text/event-stream and structured_output: json. Intermittently the final chunks stop early. Our parser throws a SyntaxError because the object ends mid-token. Example we received:
```
data: {"id":"resp_01","object":"response","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"order_id\":1234,\"status\":\"ok\"}"}},{"delta":{"content":"\n\n"}}] 
```
But in the failure case we get:
```
data: {"id":"resp_01","object":"response","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"order_id\":1234,\"status\":\"ok\"}"}},{"delta":{"content":"\n\n"}}]

data: {"id":"resp_01","object":"response","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"order_id\":1234,\"status\":\"ok\",\"meta\":{\"source\":\"api\"},\"result\":\"done\"}"}}] 
```
(note the second event ends without the final `}`)

devon_eng: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl you used and any proxy/edge (Cloudflare/NGINX/Envoy) in front of your app? Also want the response headers when it fails.

maria_cust: curl below — we use Cloudflare in front of our app, then an internal haproxy -> node backend. Timeout config is default. Headers we saw on failure: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, then shortly after `Connection: close`, and our client logs `recv: Connection reset by peer`. Curl: 
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-ops-1","mode":"json","input":"..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
```

sam_runtime: This looks like the edge or an intermediary closing the socket mid-stream. A few notes:
- SSE / chunked responses MUST have intermediary timeouts configured to allow long-lived streams. Cloudflare will terminate idle connections.
- Some proxies buffer and will coalesce chunks; others will close when they hit buffer/window limits.
- If a chunk boundary happens inside a JSON token, consumer sees truncated JSON.

jess_sre: On our side, logs show the request completed and runtime wrote the final `\n\n` event and closed normally. We see full stream in the app logs: `..."result":"done"}\n\n` before close. But in the connection traces we do see a `RST` from an intermediate net device in ~30% of failures. Suggests an intermediary (CF/haproxy) between customer and our runtime is the one dropping.

alex_support: Practical mitigations for the customer while we dig in: 1) switch to the non-streaming JSON path (single response) to avoid chunk boundaries; 2) add a simple streaming-accumulator on the client that tolerates partial events and only parse when a full JSON object is assembled (e.g., buffer until matching braces/leaders or until `\n\n` SSE terminator). Also ask them to enable TCP keepalive and increase edge timeouts.

maria_cust: We can try non-streaming but we'd lose latency benefits. Can you provide a robust client-side pattern for streaming that avoids failing on mid-chunk truncation?

devon_eng: Minimal pattern we use internally: accumulate `data:` lines into a buffer string, and only attempt JSON.parse when the buffer ends with `}\n\n` or the SSE event contains a complete top-level object. Quick pseudo:
```
let buf = '';
onChunk(chunk) {
  buf += chunk;
  // split on SSE event delimiter
  const events = buf.split('\n\n');
  for (let i = 0; i < events.length-1; i++) {
    const ev = events[i].replace(/^data:\s*/g, '');
    try { handle(JSON.parse(ev)); } catch(e) { log('parse fail, dropping event'); }
  }
  buf = events[events.length-1]; // remainder
}
```
This tolerates partial events arriving next time the socket resumes. Also implement an exponential reconnect that resumes from last known state (if request id / session token supported).

sam_runtime: We'll also add telemetry to detect whether final bytes left the runtime. If runtime indicates it wrote everything, we can point the customer to their edge. Jess, can you capture a pcap / tcpdump during a repro and check for RSTs?

jess_sre: On it. Also recommend customer set `Cache-Control: no-transform` and disable buffering on the proxy if possible (nginx: `proxy_buffering off;` / Cloudflare: disable HTTP/2 + http2-retry? will investigate).

maria_cust: Thanks — we've enabled TCP keepalive and increased Cloudflare idle timeout. We also implemented the accumulator. Will run a couple hundred streams and report. If we still see truncations we'll provide tcpdump. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Incident note created: INC-20260317-241. Link: https://redwood.infra/incidents/INC-20260317-241

alex_support: Great. Assigning follow-up tasks: @sam_runtime add write-side telemetry, @jess_sre collect pcap if customer repros, @devon_eng draft recommended client snippet for streaming JSON and add to docs. Will re-open thread when we have packet captures or if customer still sees failures. Thanks all!
